definition: CrysTBox (Crystallographic Tool Box) is a suite of computer tools designed to accelerate material research based on transmission electron microscope images via highly accurate automated analysis and interactive visualization.
details: Relying on artificial intelligence and computer vision, CrysTBox makes routine crystallographic analyses simpler, faster and more accurate compared to human evaluators. The high level of automation together with sub-pixel precision and interactive visualization makes the quantitative crystallographic analysis accessible even for non-crystallographers allowing for an interdisciplinary research. Simultaneously, experienced material scientists can take advantage of advanced functionalities for comprehensive analyses. CrysTBox is being developed in the Laboratory of electron microscopy at the Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences. For academic purposes, it is available for free. As of 2022, the suite has been deployed at research and educational facilities in more than 90 countries supporting research of ETH Zurich, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Max Planck Institutes, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Fraunhofer Institutes or Oxford University.

explainer.lead: CrysTBox is a software suite that turns transmission electron microscope images into quantitative crystallographic analyses. Its automation, sub-pixel precision and interactive visualizations help materials researchers work faster while making the analysis approachable for people without crystallography training.

tiers.eli5: A transmission electron microscope takes pictures that help scientists understand the tiny, orderly structures inside materials. CrysTBox is like a very careful measuring assistant: it examines those pictures, does many routine calculations automatically, and shows the results so people can explore them.
tiers.practitioner: Apply CrysTBox to transmission electron microscope images when routine crystallographic measurements need automation and sub-pixel precision. Use its interactive visualization to inspect results; non-crystallographers can rely on the automated workflow, while experienced materials scientists can use the advanced analysis functions.
tiers.paperLevel: CrysTBox is defined as a computer-vision and AI-based software suite mapping transmission electron microscope images to automated quantitative crystallographic analyses and interactive visualizations. Its stated performance characteristics are sub-pixel precision and improved speed and accuracy for routine analyses relative to human evaluators. It is developed at the Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences and is free for academic use.

explainer.example: A materials researcher loads a transmission electron microscope image of a specimen into CrysTBox. The suite performs the routine crystallographic measurements automatically, and the researcher uses the interactive display to inspect the results before continuing with a more comprehensive analysis.

explainer.intuition: Crystallographic image analysis involves detailed measurements that can be slow and demanding to perform manually. CrysTBox combines automated measurement with visual inspection, so the software handles routine work while the researcher can still examine and guide the analysis.
howItWorks: Provide images acquired with a transmission electron microscope.
Apply computer-vision and AI-based analysis to the image data.
Measure crystallographic features automatically with sub-pixel precision.
Inspect the measurements through interactive visualizations.
Use advanced functions when a more comprehensive analysis is needed.
explainer.whyItMatters: It reduces the manual effort behind routine crystallographic analysis and makes precise quantitative results accessible across disciplinary boundaries. At the same time, its advanced functions retain a role for experienced materials scientists conducting comprehensive studies.
misconceptions: CrysTBox is analysis software, not a transmission electron microscope.
Its automation is intended to support both non-crystallographers and experienced researchers, not to replace interactive inspection.
It is a suite of tools rather than a single crystallographic measurement.
